Using MedCP’s OMOP cohort (`n=25,587` IBD patients; Crohn’s or ulcerative colitis descendants), the most frequent extraintestinal comorbidities were:

| Extraintestinal category | IBD patients | % of IBD cohort |
|---|---:|---:|
| Arthritis / arthropathy / spondyloarthritis | 7,573 | 29.6% |
| Thromboembolism: DVT / PE | 1,311 | 5.1% |
| Skin: psoriasis / hidradenitis | 1,057 | 4.1% |
| Primary sclerosing cholangitis | 462 | 1.8% |
| Ocular inflammation: uveitis / iritis / episcleritis | 457 | 1.8% |
| Pyoderma gangrenosum | 222 | 0.9% |
| Erythema nodosum | 198 | 0.8% |

The leading signal is musculoskeletal disease, especially broad arthropathy/arthritis codes.

The MedCP knowledge graph supports a shared immune-axis explanation: IBD and common inflammatory comorbidities share genes/pathways involving cytokine–cytokine receptor signaling, T-cell receptor/activation programs, TNF/NF-κB signaling, JAK/STAT/STAT3 signaling, and the IL-23/IL-17 axis. Shared genes included `IL23R`, `IL17A`, `TNF`, `IL12B`, `IL1A`, `IL6`, `IFNG`, `STAT3`, `TYK2`, `SH2B3`, and `HLA-B`.

Interpretation: the frequent arthritis/spondyloarthritis, psoriasis, and uveitis pattern is consistent with systemic mucosal–barrier immune dysregulation, Th17/IL-23 signaling, TNF-driven inflammation, antigen presentation via HLA loci, and JAK/STAT cytokine propagation. PSC likely reflects gut–liver immune trafficking and shared epithelial/innate immune mechanisms; thromboembolism may reflect systemic inflammation–driven hypercoagulability rather than a single shared autoimmune pathway.
